plants.credit_line: Marula (Sclerocarya birrea), fruits and leaves, H5 Road south of Lower Sabie, Kruger National Park, South Africa. Photo: Bernard Dupont, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0.
plants.why: Field photograph of ripe marula fruit on the tree with diagnostic compound leaves, from Kruger NP; species named on Commons and resolution is print-ready (4000x3000).

plants.commons_title: File:Baobab (Adansonia digitata), parque nacional de Tarangire, Tanzania, 2024-05-24, DD 78.jpg
plants.credit_line: African baobab (Adansonia digitata), Tarangire National Park, Tanzania. Photo: Diego Delso, delso.photo, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.
plants.why: Iconic whole-tree habitat portrait correctly labelled Adansonia digitata, Commons Featured Picture quality at 8169x5776 px; clear species habitus for the beverage and food monograph.

plants.credit_line: Sour fig (Carpobrotus edulis), Mosteiros, Sao Miguel, Azores. Photo: Krzysztof Ziarnek (Kenraiz), Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0.
plants.why: High-resolution species photograph (4591x3443) showing diagnostic triangular succulent leaves and magenta flowers under an explicit Carpobrotus edulis label; CC BY (no ShareAlike) simplifies reuse.
plants.notes: Photographed in the Azores (Mosteiros, Sao Miguel), not in South Africa; species is naturalised there. Still a clear Carpobrotus edulis ID plate for the sour fig monograph.

plants.credit_line: Honeybush (Cyclopia genistoides), flowers, fynbos along Palmiet River, Kleinmond, Western Cape. Photo: SAplants, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0.
plants.why: No print-ready Commons bitmap was found for Cyclopia intermedia (category holds only a distribution SVG). This plate is a clearly labelled Cyclopia honeybush species (C. genistoides, Cape honeybush) in flower at 3328x4992 px from Kleinmond fynbos.
plants.notes: Fallback used: image species is Cyclopia genistoides, not C. intermedia. File kept under slug cyclopia-intermedia per monograph slot; credit and caption must name C. genistoides.

plants.credit_line: Waterblommetjie (Aponogeton distachyos) in a pond, Stellenbosch Botanical Garden, South Africa. Photo: Marco Schmidt, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0.
plants.why: Cape pondweed photographed in South Africa under the vernacular Waterblommetjies, showing floating leaves and white forked inflorescences at print-usable resolution (3456x2304).

plants.credit_line: Tsamma melon (Citrullus lanatus), Twee Rivieren Camp, Kgalagadi Transfrontier Park, South Africa. Photo: Bernard Dupont, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0.
plants.why: Wild Kalahari tsamma fruit in situ, labelled Citrullus lanatus on Commons (not a supermarket dessert melon), 4320x3240 px. Preferable to cultivated watermelon plates for the Southern African food monograph.
plants.notes: Some recent treatments place wild tsamma in Citrullus amarus; this Commons file and traditional usage retain C. lanatus.
